result.reason: Clarity: B is structured for an untrained reader — headers, one idea per paragraph, and the three ladder actions broken out as first/second/third. It translates jargon in place (duration as "how much the value of the bonds moves when interest rates move"; callable agencies as bonds that "can be called away early by the issuer"), separates quarter, YTD and trailing-12-month returns instead of massing them, and states the practical detail that the fee change is prorated on the Q4 invoice. A leaves "time-weighted total return," "strategic roll," "average duration" and "callable agency spreads were too tight" undefined, packs the performance figures into one dense block, and explains the fee cut in firm-speak ("sustainable cost," "efficient schedule") rather than in usable terms. Tone: the notes call for short, plain, and centered on yield and safety of principal for a retired couple funding two years of spending. B uses first names, states its purpose immediately, ties the short duration back to the account's job of funding the next two years, and closes with a fitting offer to walk the rungs line by line for a client who tracks yields daily. A is stiffer and institutional ("I am pleased to share") and turns the fee reduction into self-promotion ("a change... that will benefit your account," "our commitment to providing high-quality service"), which reads promotional where plainness was asked for. The drafts are comparable in length, so this is not a preference for volume; B does more work per paragraph. Accuracy was not assessed. One process note: B places the verbatim required disclosure mid-body beneath the 3.72% yield reference — contextually apt, but worth confirming against compliance convention.
